name: Arhuaco
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Tous les mots ika ont un accent. Celui-ci se manifeste par un élévation de la fréquence sonore sur une aire déterminée et/ou un renforcement de l'intensité de la prononciation sur cette même aire. [...] Nous disons alors que l'accent ika se trouve normalement sur l'avant-dernière syllabe du mot. Il s'agit bien sûr de la règle pour les mots polysyllabiques. Les monosyllabes sont normalement accentués et ce trait définit leur existence comme mot. Dans les mots de plus de trois syllabes, un accent secondaire peut apparaître. Il est alors normalement situé à deux syllabes de distance avant l'accent primaire.
new_statements.translation: All Ika words have an accent. It is realised as a rise in pitch over a given span and/or a reinforcement of intensity over that same span. [...] We therefore say that the Ika accent normally falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. This is of course the rule for polysyllabic words. Monosyllables are normally accented, and this feature defines their existence as words. In words of more than three syllables a secondary accent may appear. It is then normally located two syllables before the primary accent.
new_statements.citation: Landaburu, Jon. 1996. La langue ika ou arhuaco: phonologie. Amerindia 21. Paris: A.E.A. (CNRS-CELIA).
new_statements.locator: §1.1 'L'accent', pp. 1-2 of the journal's web PDF (Amerindia 21; original print pagination not shown in this re-typeset file)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress (pitch rise and/or intensity) falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; monosyllables are stressed. Certain bound monosyllabic grammatical morphemes (clitics, prefixes, suffixes) are invisible to the syllable count that locates stress, so surface position can deviate from strict penult; the author writes an accent mark only when stress is not in canonical (penultimate) position.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In words of more than three syllables a secondary stress may appear, normally two syllables before the primary stress (e.g. "kiNku'mʉya'ni 'he arrives', "uNkʉ'sia 'protective bracelet'); the author does not transcribe it.
new_statements.exceptions: (i) Certain bound monosyllabic grammatical morphemes (clitics, prefixes, suffixes) do not count as metrical syllables for locating the accent; (ii) to mark syntactic cohesion, words may fuse into blocks bearing a single primary accent (ko'kuru 'kawa 'it is round' vs. kokuruk'awa 'the round one'); (iii) accent is transcribed with an acute (á, í, ó) only when it is NOT in canonical penultimate position, implying some non-canonical cases exist. Landaburu 2000: 733-734 (Spanish, also saved and scanned) restates the same rule verbatim in substance: 'el acento se coloca normalmente sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra y sobre la única sílaba en caso de monosílabos'.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the word ('mot'); accent defines wordhood for monosyllables. Phrase-level: syntactically cohesive word groups can merge into a single accentual block with one primary accent. Accent is described as culminative (every word has one), realised by F0 rise and/or intensity; no claim of lexical contrast beyond the non-canonical cases.
new_statements.identity_note: Both Landaburu sources describe 'ika' = Arhuaco (arhu1242, ISO arh), Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia; Landaburu 2000 notes little internal dialect variation. No dialect restriction stated; data from Landaburu's own fieldwork (CCELA/Universidad de los Andes).

sources.note: §1.1 L'accent (PDF pp. 1-2): every word has an accent (pitch rise and/or intensity); accent normally on the penultimate syllable of the word; monosyllables accented; in words of more than three syllables a secondary accent normally two syllables before the primary; certain bound monosyllabic grammatical morphemes (clitics, prefixes, suffixes) do not count as metrical syllables for placing the accent; words may fuse into blocks with a single primary accent (ko'kuru 'kawa 'it is round' vs kokuruk'awa 'the round one'); accent is written only when not in canonical position. Later (§3, PDF p. 15)…

Santafé de Bogotá: Instituto Caro y Cuervo. (scanned PDF via Wayback copy of lenguasdecolombia.caroycuervo.gov.co; no text layer; pp. 1-3 scanned with tesseract spa at 300 dpi)
sources.note: §1.1.1.1 El acento (PDF pp. 2-3, printed pp. 733-734): 'Todas las palabras del ika llevan un acento... el acento se coloca normalmente sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra y sobre la única sílaba en caso de monosílabos. En palabras que tienen más de tres sílabas se puede dar un acento secundario situado normalmente a dos sílabas de distancia antes del acento primario... Ciertos morfemas gramaticales ligados monosilábicos (enclíticos, prefijos, sufijos) no tienen peso propio en el conteo silábico que ubica el acento.' Same analysis as 1996, in Spanish.
